sanskrit: apāṃ vyatikrame cāpi vahnirūpaṃ prakāśate tasminn uparate cāsya pītavastravad iṣyate ūrṇārūpasavarṇaṃ ca tasya rūpaṃ prakāśate
english: And when the waters are overpassed, the form of fire shines forth; and when that too has subsided, its form is said to be like a yellow garment, and a hue resembling the color of wool shines forth.

sanskrit: atha śvetāṃ gatiṃ gatvā vāyavyaṃ sūkṣmam apy ajaḥ aśuklaṃ cetasaḥ saukṣmyam avyaktaṃ brahmaṇo 'sya vai
english: Then, having attained the white course, the unborn one becomes airy and subtle—not even white—the subtlety of consciousness, the unmanifest of this Brahman.

sanskrit: eteṣv api hi jāteṣu phalajātāni me śṛṇu jātasya pārthivaiśvarye sṛṣṭir iṣṭā vidhīyate
english: And when these too are born, hear from me the fruits that arise: for one born into earthly lordship, creation is ordained as his portion.

sanskrit: prajāpatir ivākṣobhyaḥ śarīrāt sṛjati prajāḥ aṅgulyaṅguṣṭhamātreṇa hastapādena vā tathā
english: Unshakable like Prajāpati, he sends forth creatures from his body—by the measure of a finger or thumb, or likewise by hand or foot.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ kampayaty eko guṇo vāyor iti smṛtaḥ ākāśabhūtaś cākāśe savarṇatvāt praṇaśyati
english: One quality, that of wind, is remembered as making the earth tremble; and having become ether, it vanishes in the ether through sameness of nature.

sanskrit: varṇato gṛhyate cāpi kāmāt pibati cāśayān na cāsya tejasā rūpaṃ dṛśyate śāmyate tathā
english: It is grasped by its color, and at will it drinks up the receptacles; yet its form is not seen by its own radiance, and likewise it grows still.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārasya vijiteḥ pañcaite syur vaśānugāḥ ṣaṇṇām ātmani buddhau ca jitāyāṃ prabhavaty atha
english: By the conquest of the I-maker, these five become obedient to one's will; and when the sixth—the intellect within the self—is conquered, one prevails.

sanskrit: nirdoṣā pratibhā hy enaṃ kṛtsnā samabhivartate tathaiva vyaktam ātmānam avyaktaṃ pratipadyate
english: A flawless and complete illumination then attends upon him; and even so the manifest self attains to the unmanifest.

sanskrit: yato niḥsarate loko bhavati vyaktasaṃjñakaḥ tatrāvyaktamayīṃ vyākhyāṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ vistareṇa me tathā vyaktamayīṃ caiva saṃkhyāṃ pūrvaṃ nibodha me
english: That from which the world issues forth is called the manifest; there hear from me at length the exposition concerning the unmanifest, and first learn from me the reckoning of the manifest as well.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśatitattvāni tulyāny ubhayataḥ samam yoge sāṃkhye 'pi ca tathā viśeṣāṃs tatra me śṛṇu
english: The twenty-five principles are alike and equal on both sides, in Yoga and likewise in Sāṃkhya; hear from me now the distinctions therein.

sanskrit: proktaṃ tad vyaktam ity eva jāyate vardhate ca yat jīryate mriyate caiva caturbhir lakṣaṇair yutam
english: That is declared to be the manifest which is born, grows, decays, and dies—endowed with these four marks.

sanskrit: viparītam ato yat tu tad avyaktam udāhṛtam dvāv ātmānau ca vedeṣu siddhānteṣv apy udāhṛtau
english: But that which is the contrary of this is declared to be the unmanifest; and two selves are spoken of in the Vedas and likewise in the established doctrines.

sanskrit: caturlakṣaṇajaṃ tv anyaṃ caturvargaṃ pracakṣate vyaktam avyaktajaṃ caiva tathā buddham athetarat sattvaṃ kṣetrajña ity etad dvayam apy anudarśitam
english: They declare another fourfold group born of the four marks: the manifest, and that born of the unmanifest, and likewise the intelligent and the other—called sattva and the knower of the field; this pair too has been shown.

sanskrit: dvāv ātmānau ca vedeṣu viṣayeṣu ca rajyataḥ viṣayāt pratisaṃhāraḥ sāṃkhyānāṃ siddhilakṣaṇam
english: There are two selves in the Vedas, and both delight in the sense-objects; withdrawal from the object is the mark of perfection for the followers of Sāṃkhya.

sanskrit: nirmamaś cānahaṃkāro nirdvaṃdvaś chinnasaṃśayaḥ naiva krudhyati na dveṣṭi nānṛtā bhāṣate giraḥ
english: Free of 'mine,' free of the I-maker, beyond the pairs of opposites, his doubts cut away, he neither grows angry nor hates, nor does he utter false words.

sanskrit: ākruṣṭas tāḍitaś caiva maitreṇa dhyāti nāśubham vāgdaṇḍakarmamanasāṃ trayāṇāṃ ca nivartakaḥ
english: Reviled and even struck, he meditates in friendship and harbors no ill thought; he is one who turns away from all three—word, the rod, and the deeds of the mind.

sanskrit: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu brahmāṇam abhivartate naivecchati na cāniccho yātrāmātravyavasthitaḥ
english: Equal toward all beings, he draws near to Brahman; he neither desires nor is without desire, established in no more than the sustenance of life's journey.

sanskrit: alolupo 'vyatho dānto na kṛtī na nirākṛtiḥ nāsyendriyam anekāgraṃ nātikṣiptamanorathaḥ ahiṃsraḥ sarvabhūtānām īdṛk sāṃkhyo vimucyate
english: Free of greed, untroubled, self-controlled, neither a doer nor undone, his senses not scattered, his desires not flung far, harming none among all beings—such a follower of Sāṃkhya is liberated.

sanskrit: atha yogād vimucyante kāraṇair yair nibodha me yogaiśvaryam atikrānto yo 'tikrāmati mucyate
english: Now learn from me by what causes men are liberated through Yoga: he who has transcended the lordly powers of Yoga, and goes beyond them, is set free.

sanskrit: ity eṣā bhāvajā buddhiḥ kathitā te na saṃśayaḥ evaṃ bhavati nirdvaṃdvo brahmāṇaṃ cādhigacchati
english: Thus has the wisdom born of true being been told to you, beyond all doubt; in this way one becomes free of the pairs of opposites and attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca atha jñānaplavaṃ dhīro gṛhītvā śāntim āsthitaḥ unmajjaṃś ca nimajjaṃś ca jñānam evābhisaṃśrayet
english: Vyāsa said: Then the steadfast one, taking hold of the boat of knowledge and abiding in peace, whether rising up or sinking down, should take refuge in knowledge alone.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca kiṃ taj jñānam atho vidyā yayā nistarati dvayam pravṛttilakṣaṇo dharmo nivṛttir iti caiva hi
english: Śuka said: What is that knowledge, or that wisdom, by which one crosses beyond the pair—the dharma marked by engagement and the dharma marked by withdrawal?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yas tu paśyet svabhāvena vinā bhāvam acetanaḥ puṣyate ca punaḥ sarvān prajñayā muktahetukaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: But he who, insentient, would see existence apart from inherent nature, and again nourishes all things—he, freed of causes through wisdom, thrives.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ caikāntabhāvena svabhāvaḥ kāraṇaṃ matam pūtvā tṛṇabusīkāṃ vai te labhante na kiṃ cana
english: And those who hold, with single-minded conviction, that inherent nature alone is the cause—having winnowed grass and chaff, they gain nothing at all.

sanskrit: ye cainaṃ pakṣam āśritya vartayanty alpacetasaḥ svabhāvaṃ kāraṇaṃ jñātvā na śreyaḥ prāpnuvanti te
english: And those small-minded men who, taking shelter in this view, conduct themselves having deemed inherent nature the cause—they do not attain the highest good.

sanskrit: svabhāvo hi vināśāya mohakarmamanobhavaḥ niruktam etayor etat svabhāvaparabhāvayoḥ
english: For inherent nature leads to destruction, arising from delusion, action, and mind; this is the explanation of these two—inherent nature and the supreme being.

sanskrit: kṛṣyādīni hi karmāṇi sasyasaṃharaṇāni ca prajñāvadbhiḥ prakḷptāni yānāsanagṛhāṇi ca
english: For works such as plowing and the gathering of crops, and vehicles and seats and houses, have all been devised by men of wisdom.

sanskrit: ākrīḍānāṃ gṛhāṇāṃ ca gadānām agadasya ca prajñāvantaḥ pravaktāro jñānavadbhir anuṣṭhitāḥ
english: Of pleasure-gardens and houses, of diseases and of their cure, the wise are the expounders, and these things are carried out by those who possess knowledge.

sanskrit: prajñā saṃyojayaty arthaiḥ prajñā śreyo 'dhigacchati rājāno bhuñjate rājyaṃ prajñayā tulyalakṣaṇāḥ
english: Wisdom joins one to worthy ends; wisdom attains the highest good; kings enjoy their kingdoms, alike in the marks that wisdom confers.

sanskrit: pārāvaryaṃ tu bhūtānāṃ jñānenaivopalabhyate vidyayā tāta sṛṣṭānāṃ vidyaiva paramā gatiḥ
english: But the nearer and farther shore of beings is grasped by knowledge alone; for those brought into being, my son, wisdom is the supreme goal.

sanskrit: bhūtānāṃ janma sarveṣāṃ vividhānāṃ caturvidham jarāyvaṇḍam athodbhedaṃ svedaṃ cāpy upalakṣayet
english: The birth of all the manifold beings is of four kinds; one should mark it as womb-born, egg-born, then sprouting, and also sweat-born.

sanskrit: sthāvarebhyo viśiṣṭāni jaṅgamāny upalakṣayet upapannaṃ hi yac ceṣṭā viśiṣyeta viśeṣyayoḥ
english: One should mark the moving creatures as superior to the stationary; for of two things to be distinguished, that which is endowed with motion is the more distinguished.

sanskrit: āhur dvibahupādāni jaṅgamāni dvayāni ca bahupādbhyo viśiṣṭāni dvipādāni bahūny api
english: They say the moving creatures are of two kinds, the two-footed and the many-footed; and though many, the two-footed are superior to the many-footed.

sanskrit: dvipadāni dvayāny āhuḥ pārthivānītarāṇi ca pārthivāni viśiṣṭāni tāni hy annāni bhuñjate
english: They say the two-footed are of two kinds, the earthly and the others; the earthly are superior, for they consume food.

sanskrit: pārthivāni dvayāny āhur madhyamāny uttamāni ca madhyamāni viśiṣṭāni jātidharmopadhāraṇāt
english: They say the earthly are of two kinds, the middling and the highest; the middling are superior, by the holding fast of the duties of their kind.

sanskrit: madhyamāni dvayāny āhur dharmajñānītarāṇi ca dharmajñāni viśiṣṭāni kāryākāryopadhāraṇāt
english: They say the middling are of two kinds, the knowers of dharma and the others; the knowers of dharma are superior, by the holding fast of what is to be done and not done.

sanskrit: dharmajñāni dvayāny āhur vedajñānītarāṇi ca vedajñāni viśiṣṭāni vedo hy eṣu pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: They say the knowers of dharma are of two kinds, the knowers of the Veda and the others; the knowers of the Veda are superior, for in them the Veda is established.

sanskrit: vedajñāni dvayāny āhuḥ pravaktṝṇītarāṇi ca pravaktṝṇi viśiṣṭāni sarvadharmopadhāraṇāt
english: They say the knowers of the Veda are of two kinds, the expounders and the others; the expounders are superior, by the holding fast of all the dharmas.

sanskrit: vijñāyante hi yair vedāḥ sarvadharmakriyāphalāḥ sayajñāḥ sakhilā vedāḥ pravaktṛbhyo viniḥsṛtāḥ
english: For by them the Vedas are understood, with all the fruits of the rites of dharma; the Vedas, with their sacrifices and their supplements, have issued forth from the expounders.

sanskrit: pravaktṝṇi dvayāny āhur ātmajñānītarāṇi ca ātmajñāni viśiṣṭāni janmājanmopadhāraṇāt
english: They say the expounders are of two kinds, the knowers of the self and the others; the knowers of the self are superior, by the holding fast of birth and the cessation of birth.

sanskrit: dharmadvayaṃ hi yo veda sa sarvaḥ sarvadharmavid sa tyāgī satyasaṃkalpaḥ sa tu kṣāntaḥ sa īśvaraḥ
english: For he who knows the twofold dharma is wholly a knower of all dharma; he is the renouncer, true of resolve; he is the patient one, he is the lord.

sanskrit: dharmajñānapratiṣṭhaṃ hi taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaṃ pare ca kṛtaniścayam
english: For the gods know him to be the brāhmaṇa established in the knowledge of dharma, accomplished in the Brahman-of-the-word and resolved upon the Supreme.

sanskrit: antaḥsthaṃ ca bahiṣṭhaṃ ca ye ''dhiyajñādhidaivatam jānanti tān namasyāmas te devās tāta te dvijāḥ
english: Those who know the Supreme, within and without, as the principle over sacrifice and over the gods—to them we bow; they, my son, are the gods, they are the twice-born.

sanskrit: teṣu viśvam idaṃ bhūtaṃ sāgraṃ ca jagad āhitam teṣāṃ māhātmyabhāvasya sadṛśaṃ nāsti kiṃ cana
english: In them this whole world of beings, and the universe with all that is foremost in it, is set down; nothing is equal to the greatness of their being.

sanskrit: ādiṃ te nidhanaṃ caiva karma cātītya sarvaśaḥ caturvidhasya bhūtasya sarvasyeśāḥ svayaṃbhuvaḥ
english: Having wholly transcended beginning and end and action, they are lords of all the fourfold creation of beings—self-existent.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca eṣā pūrvatarā vṛttir brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate jñānavān eva karmāṇi kurvan sarvatra sidhyati
english: Vyāsa said: This earlier mode of life is ordained for the brāhmaṇa; the man of knowledge alone, while performing works, attains perfection in all things.

sanskrit: tatra cen na bhaved evaṃ saṃśayaḥ karmaniścaye kiṃ nu karma svabhāvo 'yaṃ jñānaṃ karmeti vā punaḥ
english: And if here it should not be so, a doubt arises in the determination of action: Is this action inherent nature, or is knowledge itself action?

sanskrit: tatra ceha vivitsā syāj jñānaṃ cet puruṣaṃ prati upapattyupalabdhibhyāṃ varṇayiṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: And if here there should be a wish to know whether knowledge pertains to the spirit, I shall expound it by reasoning and by perception; hear that.

sanskrit: pauruṣaṃ kāraṇaṃ ke cid āhuḥ karmasu mānavāḥ daivam eke praśaṃsanti svabhāvaṃ cāpare janāḥ
english: Some men declare human effort to be the cause in works; some praise fate, and yet other people, inherent nature.

sanskrit: pauruṣaṃ karma daivaṃ ca phalavṛttisvabhāvataḥ trayam etat pṛthagbhūtam avivekaṃ tu ke cana
english: Human effort, action, and fate, by the inherent nature of how fruits operate—this triad some hold to be separate, but some, undiscriminating, hold otherwise.

sanskrit: evam etan na cāpy evam ubhe cāpi na cāpy ubhe karmasthā viṣamaṃ brūyuḥ sattvasthāḥ samadarśinaḥ
english: 'It is thus,' 'it is not thus,' 'it is both,' and 'it is not both'—those caught in action speak unevenly, while those grounded in goodness see with an equal eye.

sanskrit: tretāyāṃ dvāpare caiva kalijāś ca sasaṃśayāḥ tapasvinaḥ praśāntāś ca sattvasthāś ca kṛte yuge
english: In the Tretā and the Dvāpara, and those born in the Kali age, are beset with doubt; but ascetics, tranquil and grounded in goodness, belong to the Kṛta age.

sanskrit: apṛthagdarśinaḥ sarve ṛksāmasu yajuḥṣu ca kāmadveṣau pṛthag dṛṣṭvā tapaḥ kṛta upāsate
english: In the Ṛc, the Sāman, and the Yajus hymns, all are seers of no division; having seen desire and hatred as distinct, they perform austerity and serve.

sanskrit: tapodharmeṇa saṃyuktas taponityaḥ susaṃśitaḥ tena sarvān avāpnoti kāmān yān manasecchati
english: Joined to the dharma of austerity, ever devoted to austerity, well disciplined, by it he attains all the desires that he wishes in his mind.

sanskrit: tapasā tad avāpnoti yad bhūtvā sṛjate jagat tadbhūtaś ca tataḥ sarvo bhūtānāṃ bhavati prabhuḥ
english: By austerity he attains that, having become which one sends forth the world; and having become that, he then becomes the lord of all beings.

sanskrit: tad uktaṃ vedavādeṣu gahanaṃ vedadarśibhiḥ vedānteṣu punar vyaktaṃ kramayogena lakṣyate
english: That has been declared, deep and hidden, in the discourses of the Veda by the seers of the Veda; and again in the Vedānta it is made manifest, discerned by the method of gradual progression.

sanskrit: ārambhayajñāḥ kṣatrasya haviryajñā viśaḥ smṛtāḥ paricārayajñāḥ śūdrāś ca japayajñā dvijātayaḥ
english: The sacrifices of the kṣatriya are those of undertaking; the vaiśyas are remembered as those whose sacrifices are oblations; the śūdras have the sacrifice of service, and the twice-born the sacrifice of muttered prayer.

sanskrit: pariniṣṭhitakāryo hi svādhyāyena dvijo bhavet kuryād anyan na vā kuryān maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate
english: For having fully accomplished his task through self-study, one becomes a brāhmaṇa; whether he does other works or does not, the friendly one is called a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tretādau sakalā vedā yajñā varṇāśramās tathā saṃrodhād āyuṣas tv ete vyasyante dvāpare yuge
english: At the beginning of the Tretā the Vedas were entire, and so the sacrifices and the orders of caste and stage of life; but through the shortening of lifespan, these are sundered in the Dvāpara age.

sanskrit: dvāpare viplavaṃ yānti vedāḥ kaliyuge tathā dṛśyante nāpi dṛśyante kaler ante punaḥ punaḥ
english: In the Dvāpara the Vedas fall into disorder, and so in the Kali age; they are seen and yet not seen, again and again, at the close of the Kali.

sanskrit: utsīdanti svadharmāś ca tatrādharmeṇa pīḍitāḥ gavāṃ bhūmeś ca ye cāpām oṣadhīnāṃ ca ye rasāḥ
english: And one's own duties decline, oppressed there by unrighteousness, along with the saps of cattle and earth and waters and the healing herbs.

sanskrit: adharmāntarhitā vedā vedadharmās tathāśramāḥ vikriyante svadharmasthāḥ sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
english: The Vedas, concealed by unrighteousness, and the Veda's dharmas and the orders of life—and creatures stationary and moving, established in their own dharma—undergo corruption.

sanskrit: yathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni vṛṣṭir bhaumāni varṣati sṛjate sarvato 'ṅgāni tathā vedā yuge yuge
english: As the rain rains down upon all earthly beings and sends forth limbs on every side, so do the Vedas, age after age.

sanskrit: visṛtaṃ kālanānātvam anādinidhanaṃ ca yat kīrtitaṃ tat purastān me yataḥ saṃyānti yānti ca
english: The diversity of time spreads forth, and that which is without beginning or end has been proclaimed by me before—that whence beings come together and to which they go.

sanskrit: dhātedaṃ prabhavasthānaṃ bhūtānāṃ saṃyamo yamaḥ svabhāvena pravartante dvaṃdvasṛṣṭāni bhūriśaḥ
english: The Ordainer is this place of origin of beings, the restraint and the restrainer; created in pairs of opposites, beings come forth abundantly by inherent nature.

sanskrit: sargaḥ kālo dhṛtir vedāḥ kartā kāryaṃ kriyā phalam etat te kathitaṃ tāta yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: Creation, time, sustenance, the Vedas, the doer, the deed, the act, and the fruit—this, my son, has been told to you, that which you asked of me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity ukto 'bhipraśasyaitat paramarṣes tu śāsanam mokṣadharmārthasaṃyuktam idaṃ praṣṭuṃ pracakrame
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, and praising this teaching of the supreme sage, joined to the meaning of the dharma of liberation, he set about to ask this.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca prajāvāñ śrotriyo yajvā vṛddhaḥ prajño 'nasūyakaḥ anāgatam anaitihyaṃ kathaṃ brahmādhigacchati
english: Śuka said: How does one who has offspring, who is learned in the Veda, a sacrificer, aged, wise, and free of envy, attain that Brahman which has not yet come and is not a matter of tradition?

sanskrit: tapasā brahmacaryeṇa sarvatyāgena medhayā sāṃkhye vā yadi vā yoge etat pṛṣṭo 'bhidhatsva me
english: By austerity, by chastity, by total renunciation, by insight, by Sāṃkhya or by Yoga—being asked this, declare it to me.

sanskrit: manasaś cendriyāṇāṃ cāpy aikāgryaṃ samavāpyate yenopāyena puruṣais tac ca vyākhyātum arhasi
english: And by what means single-pointedness of the mind and of the senses is attained by men—that too you ought to expound.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca nānyatra vidyātapasor nānyatrendriyanigrahāt nānyatra sarvasaṃtyāgāt siddhiṃ vindati kaś cana
english: Vyāsa said: Not otherwise than by knowledge and austerity, not otherwise than by restraint of the senses, not otherwise than by total renunciation does anyone find perfection.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāni sarvāṇi pūrvasṛṣṭiḥ svayaṃbhuvaḥ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ prāṇabhṛdgrāme niviṣṭāni śarīriṣu
english: All the great elements are the earlier creation of the Self-existent; they are for the most part settled within embodied beings, in the multitude of the breathing creatures.

sanskrit: bhūmer deho jalāt sāro jyotiṣaś cakṣuṣī smṛte prāṇāpānāśrayo vāyuḥ kheṣv ākāśaṃ śarīriṇām
english: From earth comes the body, from water the essence; the two eyes are remembered as from light; wind is the support of the in-breath and out-breath, and ether dwells in the cavities of embodied beings.

sanskrit: krānte viṣṇur bale śakraḥ koṣṭhe 'gnir bhuktam archati karṇayoḥ pradiśaḥ śrotre jihvāyāṃ vāk sarasvatī
english: In the stride is Viṣṇu, in strength Śakra; the fire in the belly seeks the food consumed; the intermediate quarters are in the ears for hearing, and on the tongue is the speech that is Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: karṇau tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā nāsikā caiva pañcamī darśanānīndriyoktāni dvārāṇy āhārasiddhaye
english: The two ears, the skin, the two eyes, the tongue, and the nose as the fifth—these perceivings are declared the senses, the doorways for the attainment of sustenance.

sanskrit: śabdaṃ sparśaṃ tathā rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ ca pañcamam indriyāṇi pṛthak tv arthān manaso darśayanty uta
english: Sound, touch, and likewise form, taste, and smell as the fifth—the senses, each apart, present these objects to the mind.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi mano yuṅkte vaśyān yanteva vājinaḥ manaś cāpi sadā yuṅkte bhūtātmā hṛdayāśritaḥ
english: The mind yokes the senses as a driver yokes obedient horses; and the elemental self, dwelling in the heart, ever yokes the mind as well.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ tathaiveṣāṃ sarveṣām īśvaraṃ manaḥ niyame ca visarge ca bhūtātmā manasas tathā
english: And likewise the mind is the lord of all these senses, in restraint and in release; and so is the elemental self the lord of the mind.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthāś ca svabhāvaś cetanā manaḥ prāṇāpānau ca jīvaś ca nityaṃ deheṣu dehinām
english: The senses and the objects of the senses, inherent nature, consciousness, mind, the in-breath and out-breath, and the living self—these are ever in the bodies of the embodied.

sanskrit: āśrayo nāsti sattvasya guṇaśabdo na cetanā sattvaṃ hi tejaḥ sṛjati na guṇān vai kadā cana
english: There is no abode for sattva; the word 'guṇa' is not consciousness; for sattva sends forth radiance, but never indeed the guṇas.
